props.gloss_en: wherever 'vayhi' is said, it is nothing but a term of grief
the instances: in Ahasuerus's days -- there was Haman; when the judges judged -- there was famine; when man began to multiply -- 'the Lord saw that man's wickedness was great'
more instances: Babel, Amraphel's war, the drawn sword at Jericho, Israel's trespass under Joshua, Chana's closed womb
more instances: Shmuel's sons, Saul eyeing David, 'only you shall not build the House'
the baraita: that day [the eighth day of the Tabernacle's inauguration] was joy before the Holy One as the day heaven and earth were created -- 'vayhi' here (Lev 9:1), 'vayhi' there (Gen 1:5)
the verses cited against the dictum: the 480th year (1 Kings 6:1), Jacob seeing Rachel (Gen 29:10), 'it was evening and it was morning, one day' -- and the second, and the third, and many more
Rav Ashi: every 'vayhi' -- there are [some] this way and [some] that way
Rav Ashi: 'vayhi bimei' (and it was in the days of) is nothing but a term of grief
there are five 'vayhi bimei': Ahasuerus, the judges, Amraphel, Ahaz, Jehoiakim
R' Levi, a tradition from our fathers: Amotz and Amatzya were brothers
R' Yonatan: every bride who is modest in her father-in-law's house merits that kings and prophets issue from her
whence? from Tamar, as it is written: 'Judah saw her and thought her a harlot, for she had covered her face' (Gen 38:15)
because she covered her face he thought her a harlot? rather: because she covered her face in her father-in-law's house and he did not know her, she merited that kings and prophets issued from her
kings -- from David
prophets -- for R' Levi said: Amotz and Amatzya were brothers, and it is written 'the vision of Isaiah son of Amotz' (Isa 1:1)
R' Levi, a tradition from our fathers: the place of the Ark is not part of the measure
the baraita: the Ark that Moses made had ten cubits on every side
and it is written: the Sanctuary twenty cubits long (1 Kings 6:20), and each cherub's wing ten cubits -- where did the Ark itself stand? rather, learn from it: it stood by a miracle
R' Yonatan opened this passage from here: 'I will rise against them... and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendant' (Isa 14:22)
'name' -- this is the script
'remnant' -- this is the language
'offspring' -- this is the kingship
'descendant' -- this is Vashti
RSbN opened from here: 'instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress, and instead of the nettle the myrtle' (Isa 55:13)
'instead of the thorn' -- instead of wicked Haman, who made himself an idol
as it is written: 'and upon all the thorns and upon all the brambles' (Isa 7:19)
'shall come up the cypress' -- this is Mordechai, who is called the head of all spices
as it is said: 'take the chief spices, flowing myrrh [mor dror]' (Ex 30:23), which we translate 'mira dachya'
'instead of the nettle' -- instead of wicked Vashti, granddaughter of Nebuchadnezzar, who burned the covering [refidat] of the House of the Lord
as it is written: 'its covering of gold' (Song 3:10)
'shall come up the myrtle' -- this is righteous Esther, who is called Hadassah
as it is said: 'and he brought up Hadassah' (Est 2:7)
'and it shall be to the Lord for a name' -- this is the reading of the Megilla
'for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off' -- these are the days of Purim
RYbL opened from here: 'as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, so will He rejoice... to do you evil' (Deut 28:63)
the verse RYbL opens with, as read plainly: the Lord rejoices over Israel's downfall
R' Yochanan: why is 'for He is good' not said in this thanksgiving (II Chr 20:21)? because the Holy One does not rejoice in the downfall of the wicked
R' Yochanan: 'and the one came not near the other all the night' (Ex 14:20) -- the ministering angels wished to sing; the Holy One said: My handiwork is drowning in the sea, and you sing?
R' Elazar: He does not rejoice, but He causes others to rejoice
the wording is precise too: it is written 'yasis' (causes to rejoice), not 'yasus' (rejoices)
R' Abba bar Kahana opened from here: 'to the man who is good before Him He gives wisdom, knowledge and joy' (Eccl 2:26)
'the man who is good before Him' -- this is righteous Mordechai
'and to the sinner He gives the task of gathering and heaping up' -- this is Haman
'to give to him that is good before God' -- this is Mordechai and Esther
as it is written: 'and Esther set Mordechai over the house of Haman' (Est 8:2)
Rabbah bar Ofran opened from here: 'I will set My throne in Elam and destroy from there king and princes' (Jer 49:38)
'king' -- this is Vashti
'and princes' -- this is Haman and his ten sons
Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak opened from here: 'for we are slaves, yet in our bondage our God has not forsaken us, but extended mercy to us before the kings of Persia' (Ezra 9:9)
when? in the time of Haman
R' Chanina bar Pappa opened from here: 'You caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water' (Ps 66:12)
'through fire' -- in the days of wicked Nebuchadnezzar
'and through water' -- in the days of Pharaoh
'and You brought us out to abundance' -- in the days of Haman
R' Yochanan opened from here: 'He remembered His mercy and faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God' (Ps 98:3)
when did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? in the days of Mordechai and Esther
Reish Lakish opened from here: 'a roaring lion and a ravenous bear, so is a wicked ruler over a poor people' (Prov 28:15)
'a roaring lion' -- this is wicked Nebuchadnezzar
as it is written of him: 'the lion has come up from his thicket' (Jer 4:7)
'a ravenous bear' -- this is Ahasuerus
as it is written of him: 'and behold another beast, a second, like a bear' (Dan 7:5)
Rav Yosef taught: these are the Persians, who eat and drink like a bear, are fleshy like a bear, grow hair like a bear, and have no rest like a bear
'a wicked ruler' -- this is Haman
'over a poor people' -- these are Israel, who are poor in mitzvot
R' Elazar opened from here: 'through slothfulness the rafters sink, and through idleness of hands the house leaks' (Eccl 10:18)
because of Israel's slothfulness in not occupying themselves with Torah, the enemy of the Holy One (a euphemism) became poor
and 'mach' means only poor, as it is said: 'but if he be too poor for your valuation' (Lev 27:8)
and 'mekareh' (rafters) means only the Holy One, as it is said: 'who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters' (Ps 104:3)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak opened from here: 'had it not been the Lord who was for us... when a man rose up against us' (Ps 124:1-2)
'a man' -- and not a king
Rava opened from here: 'when the righteous increase the people rejoice, and when the wicked rule the people sigh' (Prov 29:2)
'when the righteous increase the people rejoice' -- this is Mordechai and Esther
as it is written: 'and the city of Shushan shouted and was glad' (Est 8:15)
'when the wicked rule the people sigh' -- this is Haman
as it is written: 'and the city of Shushan was perplexed' (Est 3:15)
Rav Matna said: from here -- 'for what great nation has God so near to it' (Deut 4:7)
Rav Ashi said: from here -- 'or has God tried to go and take Him a nation from the midst of another nation' (Deut 4:34)
Rav: 'vayhi' -- 'vai' and 'hei' (woe and lament)
that is what is written: 'and there you shall sell yourselves to your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen' (Deut 28:68)
Shmuel: [from here] 'I will not reject them, nor abhor them, to destroy them utterly' (Lev 26:44)
Shmuel: 'I will not reject them' -- in the days of the Greeks
'nor abhor them' -- in the days of Nebuchadnezzar
'to destroy them utterly' -- in the days of Haman
'to break My covenant with them' -- in the days of the Persians
'for I am the Lord their God' -- in the days of Gog and Magog
the baraita: 'I will not reject them' -- in the days of the Chaldeans, when I raised for them Daniel, Chananya, Mishael and Azarya
'nor abhor them' -- in the days of the Greeks, when I raised Shimon HaTzaddik, the Hasmonean and his sons, and Mattityahu the High Priest
'to destroy them utterly' -- in the days of Haman, when I raised Mordechai and Esther
'to break My covenant with them' -- in the days of the Romans, when I raised those of the house of Rabbi and the sages of the generations
'for I am the Lord their God' -- in the time to come, when no nation or tongue will be able to rule over them
R' Levi: from here -- 'but if you will not drive out the inhabitants of the land' (Num 33:55)
R' Chiyya: from here -- 'and as I thought to do to them, so will I do to you' (Num 33:56)
Rav: Ahasuerus -- the brother of the 'head', the brother of wicked Nebuchadnezzar who is called 'head'
as it is said: 'you are the head of gold' (Dan 2:38)
and the peer of the 'head': he [Nebuchadnezzar] killed -- this one sought to kill; he destroyed -- this one sought to destroy
as it is said: 'and in the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem' (Ezra 4:6)
Shmuel: [so called] because Israel's faces were blackened in his days like the bottom of a pot
R' Yochanan: whoever remembers him says 'woe for his head'
R' Chanina: because all became poor in his days
as it is said: 'and King Ahasuerus laid a tribute' (Est 10:1)
'he is Ahasuerus' -- he is in his wickedness from beginning to end; so 'he is Esau', 'he is Datan and Aviram', 'he is King Ahaz'
'Avram, he is Avraham' -- he is in his righteousness from beginning to end; 'he is Aharon and Moshe' -- likewise
'and David, he is the youngest' -- he is in his smallness from beginning to end: as in his youth he made himself small before one greater in Torah, so in his reign before one greater in wisdom
Rav: 'who reigned' -- he reigned by himself [not by inheritance]
some say it to his credit: there was no one as fit to be king as he
and some say it to his disgrace: he was not fit for kingship, and gave much money and rose
one said: Hodu is at one end of the world and Kush at the other end
and one said: Hodu and Kush are next to each other; as he ruled over Hodu and Kush, so he ruled from one end of the world to the other
similarly: 'for he had dominion over all the region beyond the river, from Tifsach to Aza' (1 Kings 5:4) -- one said: Tifsach at one end of the world and Aza at the other
and one said: Tifsach and Aza are next to each other; as he [Solomon] ruled over them, so he ruled over the whole world
Rav Chisda: '127 provinces' -- at first he ruled over seven, then over twenty, and finally over a hundred
if so: 'and the years of Amram's life were seven and thirty and a hundred years' (Ex 6:20) -- what would you expound in it?

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני הכא דקרא יתירא הוא: מכדי כתיב מהודו ועד כוש, שבע ועשרים ומאה מדינה למה לי? שמע מינה לדרשה
